newsitem.title: VATICAN: Vatican says Albanian deaths "avoidable tragedy".
newsitem.headline: Vatican says Albanian deaths "avoidable tragedy".

text.p: The Vatican said on Saturday that the deaths of Albanian refugees whose ship sank in the Adriatic sea were an "avoidable tragedy" and criticised bureaucracy and what it called international indifference.

Italian navy officials recovered four bodies and rescued 34 people after an ageing Albanian harbour patrol boat collided with a navy corvette that was trying to intercept it in international waters on Friday.
It was not known how many Albanians had been on board the boat and survivors feared many more died.

"A new tragedy that weighs upon the bureaucratic slowness and indifference of a part of the international community," declared the semi-official Vatican newspaper L'Osservatore Romano under the headline "an avoidable tragedy".
"It is necessary and urgent to help the Albanian people because every lost day brings catastrophe closer," it said.
L'Osservatore quoted Roman Catholic Archbishop Cosmo Ruppi of the southern Italian city of Lecce saying that the Church had been calling for swift action to help Albania.
"Time has been lost talking, making diplomatic contacts and having meetings and more meetings when the Albanian situation called for rapid, decisive, massive intervention," the archbishop said.
Settimo Todisco, the archbishop of the Italian port of Brindisi, also accused the international community of failing to tackle the Albanian crisis.
"What happened in the sea last night should make the European Union and the United Nations ask themselves why they are not acting," he said.
The U.N. security council gave the go ahead on Saturday for Italy to organize a multinational force to Albania to guard deliveries of food and medicine.
Some EU countries, notably Britain and Germany, have said they are against any military intervention.

Albania was thrown into chaos early this month when armed bands took over the south of the country following protests blaming the government for the collapse of a fraudulent investment scheme in which entire savings were wiped out.
More than 13,000 people have fled to Italy since then on a flotilla of rusty and ancient boats.
